newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani banks say repo rate cut to help economy.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani banks say repo rate cut to help economy.

text.p: Pakistan's four major banks said on Wednesday a central bank decision to lower repo rate would help the economy, alleviate liquidity problems and boost savings.
On Tueasday, the central bank reduced its key three-day repo rate against short-term federal bonds and federal investment bonds to an annualised 19 percent from 20 percent.
The rate, last changed on October 22, determines the interest charged by the central bank on amounts provided as temporary funding facility to commercial banks.

"The cut in the repo rate will lead to a reduction in the mark-up (interest) in the short term," Shaukat Tareen, president of the state-run Habib Bank Ltd, told a news conference. Three other heads of commercial banks present expressed similar views.
The interest rate is likely to fall to 20 percent from the present 24 percent, Tareen said.
